title: Burst priming stall: coordinated emergency fix for kernel preemption causing short-session token starvation
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: Over the past 48 hours several enterprise customers and internal SLO monitors reported sharp degradations in initial token throughput (tokens/sec for short sessions) across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments. Symptom profile: 200–800ms extra first-token latency on short prompts (<= 64 tokens) and >30% drop in tokens/sec for sessions with multi-model fanout. Root cause (initial hypothesis): an aggressive kernel preemption heuristic introduced in runtime-1.21 (kernel selection heuristic #B) causes priming kernels to be preempted by large background workloads on heterogeneous GPUs. The effect is amplified for quantized int8 kernels and mixed model fanouts where small priming kernels are evicted mid-emit and must be re-dispatched, causing repeated warmups and token starvation. This ticket coordinates immediate mitigation, customer communication, rollback and follow-ups.
updates: 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC — Pager alerts triggered for hosted-region-us-east-1 SLOs; initial triage by on-call; identified pattern correlated with recent kernel selector rollout (runtime-1.21).

2026-03-10 11:05 UTC — Customer A (fintech) escalated after repeated timeouts in their quick-chat feature; provided traces and model IDs. Eng on-call (Ravi) reproduced in staging with trace IDs and kernel histograms.

2026-03-11 02:45 UTC — Reproduced locally: small priming kernels (<= 120ms) were being preempted by long fusion kernels; eviction path caused KV warmup to restart. Hypothesis created and safety rollback planned.

2026-03-11 07:30 UTC — Emergency rollback of kernel preemption heuristic performed in hosted us-east-1 and dedicated pools (canary then full). Initial telemetry shows first-token latency improvement ~60% on affected models.

2026-03-12 16:00 UTC — Private customer cluster (Customer B) reported residual token throughput oscillation; deployed secondary mitigations (reserve small stream pool for priming and throttle large background batchers).

2026-03-13 10:20 UTC — Rolled out emergency patch (PR #4256) that adds a preemption-safe path for priming kernels and a microbackoff for evicted priming tasks. Deployed to canary; monitoring for regressions.

2026-03-14 14:55 UTC — Metrics: hosted global short-session tokens/sec recovered to within 95% of baseline; dedicated clusters show 90–98% recovery depending on model quantization. Customer bridge ongoing for two enterprise customers.
2026-03-15 08:10 UTC — Rolling plan: keep preemption-rollback in place until a more robust scheduler is implemented; begin work on long-term fixes under runtime-scheduler-redesign epic.
action_items: Continue customer bridge until affected customers confirm recovery (assignee: Ravi).
Backfill missing priming kernel telemetry in private clusters (owner: Observability team).
Implement deterministic preemption bypass for priming kernels (owner: runtime/scheduler team).
Add test harness to reproduce mixed-quantization fanout preemption locally (owner: perf-team).
Draft customer postmortem and outage summary for NRR and affected enterprises (owner: Ops).
Schedule design review for scheduler redesign RFC (target: 2026-03-22).
acceptance_criteria: Short-session first-token latency returns to <= 1.1x baseline across Hosted/Dedicated/Private on representative models (verification via e2e jobs).
Tokens/sec for <64-token sessions recovers to >= 95% of pre-regression baseline in production telemetry.
Customers in active bridge confirm functional recovery and sign off on mitigation plan.
Follow-up sprint tickets created for long-term fixes with owners and estimates.
